Talking stage
TAWK-ing stayj
noun phrase (Gen-Z slang)
From English talk and stage. The phrase arose among American teenagers on Twitter and Snapchat in the mid-2010s (c. 2015–2017) for the period of texting, flirting, and spending time together before two people call themselves a couple, and it was standard TikTok vocabulary by about 2020 ("we’re just talking," "stuck in the talking stage"). It displaced older phrases like seeing someone and going steady; a grandparent’s nearest equivalent is courting, which had a destination the talking stage lacks.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

In current slang the talking stage is the undefined season before dating: two people text every day, flirt, perhaps spend time together, but neither has said what this is, and either can drift away without a word. It can last weeks or months, run alongside other "talking stages," and end in ghosting rather than goodbye. The Christian observation: getting to know someone before marriage is wise, and Scripture is warm toward a man who seeks a wife, for "Whoso findeth a wife findeth a good thing" (Pro 18:22). The trouble is not the talking; it is a stage with no exit. It lets hearts be stirred while no one is responsible for them, and the Song warns, "stir not up, nor awake my love, till he please" (Son 2:7). It trains young people to keep their options open and their words vague, when Christ said, "let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay" (Mat 5:37). Rebekah was asked one plain question, "Wilt thou go with this man?" and gave one plain answer: "I will go" (Gen 24:58). Paul wants every believer to know how to keep himself "in sanctification and honour" (1Th 4:4), and honour includes not toying with another person’s affections. A father tells his son: if you are not ready to say what your intentions are, you are not ready to be messaging her every night; and if you are, say it, to her and to her father. He tells his daughter: a young man who will only "talk" for months has already told you how much he is willing to give.

Webster 1828 Definition

Gen-Z slang (Twitter / Snapchat c. 2015, TikTok-standard by 2020) for the undefined pre-dating season of texting and flirting — a season Scripture would fill with plain intentions, honour, and a yes that means yes.

expand to see more

TALKING STAGE, n. phr. (Gen-Z slang, c. 2015–present; American teen social media) The undefined period of texting, flirting, and spending time together before two people call themselves a couple. "We’re not dating, we’re in the talking stage."

Talking, v.i., in the same sense: "Are you two talking?" Stuck in the talking stage, a relationship that never becomes defined. Talking to several people at once is common and accepted in the slang.

A grandparent’s nearest words: courting, keeping company, going steady — each of which named a stage with an aim.

Webster (1828), root word talk: “TALK, verb intransitive tauk. 1. To converse familiarly; to speak, as in familiar discourse, when two or more persons interchange thoughts. I will buy with you, sell with you, talk with you; but I will not eat with you. In Aesop's time When all things talk'd, and talk'd in rhyme. I will come down and talk with thee. Numbers 11:17.”

Decode for parents: "we’re just talking" can mean hours of private messages a night with no one, including the two of them, accountable for where it is going.

Key Scripture

Pro 18:22 — "Whoso findeth a wife findeth a good thing, and obtaineth favour of the LORD."

Son 2:7 — "I charge you, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, and by the hinds of the field, that ye stir not up, nor awake my love, till he please."

Mat 5:37 — "But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil."

Gen 24:58 — "And they called Rebekah, and said unto her, Wilt thou go with this man? And she said, I will go."

1Th 4:4 — "That every one of you should know how to possess his vessel in sanctification and honour;"

Modern Corruption

The talking stage keeps hearts engaged and intentions undeclared, so that affection can be stirred, shared, and dropped without anyone owning a word of it.

expand to see more

Every generation has had a season between strangers and spouses; what is new is a season designed to commit to nothing. The talking stage lets a boy and a girl share their days, their secrets, and their late-night messages while either may say, at any moment, that it was never anything. It is often run with two or three others in parallel, and it often ends not with a conversation but with silence. The Song of Solomon counsels the opposite pace: "stir not up, nor awake my love, till he please" (Son 2:7) — do not wake what you are not ready to keep.

Scripture’s courtships are short on ambiguity. Abraham’s servant states his errand before he eats; Rebekah answers, "I will go" (Gen 24:58); Boaz settles the matter at the gate before witnesses the same day. Christ’s rule for speech, "Yea, yea; Nay, nay" (Mat 5:37), binds the heart as much as the marketplace. Teach your children that getting to know someone is good and that leaving someone guessing is unkind; a young man who means it will say so, and a family that loves its daughter will ask him to.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Middle English talken (to converse) + stage (a step or period) → mid-2010s teen social media: talking, the pre-dating phase → c. 2020 TikTok: the talking stage.

expand to see more

Middle English talken — to converse, related to tale and tell

Old French estage — a standing place, a floor; English stage, a step in a process

2000s: talking to someone, a soft phrase for early romantic interest

c. 2015–2017 Twitter and Snapchat: the talking stage

c. 2020 TikTok: the stage nobody leaves, and the ghosting that ends it

Usage

""We’ve been in the talking stage since August and he still hasn’t asked me out.""

"Let your yea be yea, in courtship too (Mat 5:37)."

"Do not wake a love you are not ready to keep (Son 2:7)."
